WITH scan_site_join AS (
  SELECT s.gbsize, s.spanmin, z.riskeval
  FROM scans s
  INNER JOIN sites z ON s.zoneref = z.zoneregistry
),
group_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    riskeval, 
    AVG(gbsize / spanmin) AS rate
  FROM scan_site_join
  WHERE gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY riskeval
),
benchmark_value AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS bench FROM group_rates
)
SELECT 
  AVG(gr.rate) AS avg_rate,
  AVG(gr.rate - bv.bench) AS avg_excess
FROM group_rates gr
CROSS JOIN benchmark_value bv
WHERE gr.rate > bv.bench

assumptions.assumption: When no groups have a rate strictly above the benchmark, the query returns zero rows rather than a single row containing NULL values. The request's phrasing "return one row with two values" describes the structure of output when groups exist above the benchmark, not a guarantee of always producing a row.
